# Six-Week Operations Analytics — Management Brief

**Scope:** The only factual input is `input/operations.csv` — 18 weekly records (weeks W01–W06) across three teams: Atlas, Birch, Cedar. No records were added, inferred or converted; the CSV was read only and remains byte-identical.

## Method

All figures below were recomputed independently from the raw integer columns of `input/operations.csv`, aggregating raw counts and minutes first and rounding only once, at final serialization, to two decimal places. Rounded percentages were never summed or re-averaged.

- **Completion percent** = completed_orders ÷ work_orders × 100
- **Minutes per completed order** = actual_minutes ÷ completed_orders
- **Schedule variance (minutes)** = actual_minutes − planned_minutes (positive = over plan)
- Integer metrics (work_orders, completed_orders, defects, planned_minutes, actual_minutes, schedule_variance_minutes) are exact sums of the weekly rows.

## Overall findings

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Work orders | 233 |
| Completed orders | 217 |
| Defects | 18 |
| Planned minutes | 14,985 |
| Actual minutes | 15,440 |
| Completion | 93.13% |
| Minutes per completed order | 71.15 |
| Schedule variance | +455 minutes (over plan) |

The portfolio delivered 93.13% of planned work orders while running 455 minutes (≈3.0% of planned time) over plan — the small variance is entirely attributable to one team.

## Per-team findings

| Team | Work orders | Completed | Completion | Defects | Planned min | Actual min | Min/completed | Variance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Atlas | 95 | 89 | 93.68% | 7 | 5,700 | 5,780 | 64.94 | +80 |
| Birch | 75 | 71 | 94.67% | 3 | 4,875 | 4,910 | 69.15 | +35 |
| Cedar | 63 | 57 | 90.48% | 8 | 4,410 | 4,750 | 83.33 | +340 |

**Completion.** Birch leads at 94.67%, Atlas is close behind at 93.68%, and Cedar trails at 90.48% — a 4.19-point spread. Cedar is also the only team that missed more than one order in a week (W05: 10 of 12) and accounts for 6 of the 16 total uncompleted orders.

**Defects.** 18 defects in total. Atlas carries 7 (7.4% of its 95 orders), Cedar carries 8 on only 63 orders (12.7%), and Birch is markedly cleaner with 3 defects on 75 orders (4.0%). Cedar's defect rate is roughly 3× Birch's.

**Schedule variance.** Atlas (+80) and Birch (+35) are effectively on plan. Cedar alone accounts for 340 of the 455 over-plan minutes — about 75% of the total variance while contributing only 27% of work orders. Cedar also has the slowest throughput at 83.33 minutes per completed order versus 64.94 for Atlas and 69.15 for Birch, a 28% gap against Atlas.

## Executive recommendation

Direct the next improvement cycle at Cedar, not the portfolio: Cedar is the single root cause of three of the four weak signals — lowest completion (90.48%), highest defect concentration (12.7% of orders), and 75% of all schedule overrun with the worst minutes-per-completed-order (83.33). Atlas and Birch need no corrective action at this granularity; protect their current practice as the benchmark. Specifically, review Cedar's W05 (10/12 completed, +80 minutes over plan) and W04 (7/8 completed, 560 planned vs 610 actual) to identify whether the overrun is a scoping/estimation problem or a rework problem — the high defect count alongside high minutes points toward rework. If Cedar were brought to Birch's 4.0% defect rate and 69.15 minutes per completed order, the portfolio would recover roughly 300 of the 455 over-plan minutes with no change to Atlas or Birch. Because the dataset covers only six weeks and three teams, this recommendation should be re-tested on a longer window before any resourcing decision.

## Verification note

Every metric in this brief was recomputed from the raw CSV integers before comparison with the approved expected values; all 32 numeric fields matched with zero discrepancies. Parsed data rows: 18 (header plus 18 records), matching the expected `row_count` of 18. `input/operations.csv` was read only and not modified.
